evidence.policy: decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 0 to 1/4 percent
evidence.balance_sheet: increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $500 billion and its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $200 billion
evidence.inflation: overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent
evidence.labour: the unemployment rate has remained low
evidence.growth: The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook
evidence.guidance_diff: expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events

supporting_statement: As a central bank policy economist focused on the dual mandate, the unprecedented emergency response—slashing the policy rate by 150 basis points to the 0-0.25% lower bound and launching massive open-market asset purchases—reflects an aggressive reaction function to the severe macroeconomic and financial shock from the coronavirus outbreak. With inflation running below target and looming downside risks to employment and economic activity, monetary policy has pivoted decisively to an extreme easing stance.
